business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Employer of Record and Cross-Border Contractor Payroll

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China (Hong Kong SAR)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: common law jurisdiction within a civil-law sovereign; English common law and equity continue under Article 8 of the Basic Law of the HKSAR, supplemented by HKSAR local statutes.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) and its supplementary agreements
Arrangement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Hong Kong: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Ordinance (Cap. 615), Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37), Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), and Employment Agencies Regulation (Cap. 57A). For China-linked UBOs: Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities, jointly issued by PBOC and SAMR as Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry / Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: path A for Hague Apostille Convention member states - certified copy issued by the Companies Registry, followed by an Apostille certificate from the designated HKSAR Competent Authority; path B for non-member states - certified copy, then authentication by the competent foreign-affairs authority, then consular legalization by the destination-state consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Current Status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry / Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: path A for Apostille Convention states - official registry certificate, then Apostille by the HKSAR designated Competent Authority; path B for non-Apostille states - official registry certificate, then foreign-affairs authentication, then consular legalization at the destination-state consulate. The two paths are never combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing local formation agents and counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / general partners of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: notarize the resolution or power of attorney before a Hong Kong notary public; for Apostille Convention states, attach an Apostille from the designated HKSAR Competent Authority; for non-convention states, complete foreign-affairs authentication and consular legalization at the destination consulate. No chain of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Limited Partnership Agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General and limited partners executing the Foreign-Invested Partnership agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: execute, notarize, and then either (A) apply for an Apostille through the HKSAR designated Competent Authority for Apostille Convention states, or (B) obtain authentication by the competent foreign-affairs authority and consular legalization at the destination consulate for non-member states. These are alternative routes, never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a licensed Hong Kong bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Hong Kong bank maintaining or proposed to maintain the payroll and operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: original bank letter on bank letterhead with authorized signature; for Apostille Convention states, the notarized bank letter is apostilled by the HKSAR designated Competent Authority; for non-member states, the notarized bank letter is authenticated by the competent foreign-affairs authority and then consularized by the destination-state consulate. Apostille and consular legalization paths are mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All natural-person UBOs, general and limited partners, authorised signatories, direct and indirect holders at or above the 25% threshold, and payroll beneficiaries must be screened before onboarding against the HKMA/JFIU Combined Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, HM Treasury sanctions list, and PRC Foreign Ministry sanctions. PEPs, their family members, and close associates are identified through risk-based checks, including adverse-media searches, source-of-wealth verification, enhanced due diligence, transaction monitoring, and mandatory escalation. Screening is repeated on a rolling basis and before every payroll disbursement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry and ICRIS name search and reservation portal; Business Registration Office e-Registration portal of the Inland Revenue Department.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Hong Kong entity may carry one English name, one Chinese name, or both. The Chinese name must be in Traditional Chinese characters; simplified characters are not accepted for the statutory name. The four-tier naming convention comprises: (1) entity type prefix, (2) distinctive core element, (3) business-nature qualifier, and (4) legal-form suffix. Phonetic transliteration is allowed but must not create a mark that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing register entry and must not imply government connection, professional licence, or regulated financial activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written review request with the Companies Registry within 14 days, quoting the proposed name and the rejection reference, and providing evidence that the name is not prohibited, not identical or too similar to an existing registered name, and that any sensitive token has been approved by the relevant authority. The Registry will review and issue a decision; if the rejection is upheld, the applicant may challenge the decision by judicial review at the Court of First Instance within 28 days. The incorporation filing may be suspended while the review is pending, and rejected-name fees are not refundable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is technically available for registered-office purposes in Hong Kong if it provides a physical street address for service of process and document retention, but it is not recommended for this industry. The Inland Revenue Department will not regard a virtual office as a sufficient place of business for tax residence or profits tax purposes; the Labour Department requires a genuine office for an employment agency licence; banks and payment service providers such as Wise normally require operating evidence and local payroll administration. Therefore a dedicated serviced office with local staff, payroll records, and licences is the expected compliance standard.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for inspection: (1) employment agency licence displayed at the registered office; (2) original or certified payroll contracts, MPF records, and employment records; (3) fee schedules and client contracts; (4) personal data privacy policy; (5) lease, utility, and staffing records evidencing the registered place of business. Likelihood: high, about 70-80%, of an unannounced Labour Department inspection within the first 12 months; the Inland Revenue Department and Companies Registry may also conduct random venue visits under the Inland Revenue Ordinance and the Companies Ordinance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation filing fee for Foreign-Invested Partnership
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry, Government of the HKSAR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) fee schedule plus official levy.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Labour Department, Government of the HKSAR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory licence fee under Employment Agencies Regulation (Cap. 57A); annual renewal is separate.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening, and name clearance workstream
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Hong Kong law firm and AML compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee for stage 1 due diligence; not a statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille bundle for the five mandatory instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Hong Kong notary public and the designated Apostille Competent Authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary fee tariff plus Apostille certificate fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Serviced registered office and local commercial substance arrangement, first year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual market rate for a physical business-centre office in Hong Kong.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified name search and Certificate of Good Standing procurement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry, Government of the HKSAR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cap. 622K search, certification, and certified copy tariff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Limited Partnerships Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637) sections 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11 and 15; the Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 352) sections 2 to 29; the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) section 5; the Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57) Part XII; the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) sections 51, 52 and 54; the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Ordinance (Cap. 615) Schedule 1. The Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China articles 3, 4 and 13 to 16 are applied solely for establishing the foreign-invested status and reporting lineage of the ultimate PRC parent investor; the domestic formation and governance law is that of the Hong Kong SAR.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Limited Partnerships Fund Unit, through the e-Registry online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LPF1 Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership Fund, together with Form IRBR1 Business Registration Application, filed under the Limited Partnerships Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637) and the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - no statutory minimum paid-up capital or blocked escrow account rule applies to a Limited Partnership Fund under Cap. 637. The partners fix the capital in the Limited Partnership Agreement; contributions may be paid directly into the designated partnership bank account and are callable or repayable only in accordance with the Limited Partnership Agreement and the preservation-of-assets and solvency protections in Cap. 637. For PRC investor outbound filing, any capital remittance must be reported under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange and foreign direct investment regulations if routed through mainland China, but that condition is not a formation capital blockade at the Hong Kong registry level.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IN THE MATTER OF [NAME OF PARTNERSHIP], a Foreign-Invested Partnership proposed to be formed in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and in the matter of the Limited Partnerships Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637), the Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 352), the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), the Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57), the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Ordinance (Cap. 615), and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China as to the ultimate investing partner; RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS / PARTNERS' MANAGEMENT BOARD; By unanimous written consent, the initial partners and proposed statutory officers resolve as follows: (1) Registered Office. RESOLVED that the registered office at [full Hong Kong address] be and is adopted as the statutory registered office, and the General Partner is authorized to execute the consent of owner, lease, and all required registrations. (2) Subscription of Capital. RESOLVED that the initial aggregate capital subscription of [currency and amount] be subscribed by the foreign corporate partner and included as the contributed capital of the Partnership; the Managing Partner is authorized to call, receive, and apply capital contributions and to maintain contribution records; no capital may be returned to partners except upon the solvency, creditor notice, and preservation conditions required by Cap. 637. (3) Banking Authorization. RESOLVED that [bank] be appointed as principal banker; the General Partner and [authorized signatory] are authorized, jointly for any two signatures, to open, maintain, and operate bank accounts, configure Local Payroll Direct Debit and Wise payment rails, sign checks, undertake payroll mandates, and accept funds; banking authorities continue until revoked by later resolution. (4) Statutory Officers. RESOLVED that [name] is appointed General Partner with exclusive management powers; [name] is appointed Responsible Person for AML/CFT purposes; [name] is appointed Employment Agency Authorized Representative; [name] is appointed Data and Compliance Officer; and [name] is appointed Tax Representative for all Inland Revenue Ordinance matters. (5) Government Filings. RESOLVED that the General Partner is authorized to file the Form LPF1, Form IRBR1, Employment Agency Licence application, and all statutory declarations and supporting documents with the Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, and Labour Department. (6) General Implementation. RESOLVED that all lawful acts performed by the appointees incidental to registration, bank account opening, licensing, and commencement of EOR payroll services before the date of this resolution are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Pre-Formation Compliance Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry Hong Kong e-Registry portal and Hong Kong Trade and Industry Department for any foreign-invested name endorsement if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an advanced name search through the e-Registry module to determine that the proposed English name and optional Chinese name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership do not conflict with existing registered companies, Limited Partnership Fund registrations, or trademarks of striking similarity. Check the proposed name for prohibited words, government endorsement requirements, and misleading character under Cap. 637 section 7 and the Trade Marks Ordinance (Cap. 32). If the proposed name includes terms suggesting banking, insurance, trust, or specialized manpower licensing, obtain prior written consent from the relevant statutory authority. Secure a written trademark clearance opinion if target payment rails and branding will rely on the name. Retain the name search result in the formation file. Confirm that the proposed registered office street address is a physical Hong Kong premises and not a post-office box, and verify that the landlord permits the intended employment agency and EOR payroll operation.
required_dossiers: Proposed English and Chinese partnership name
Signed name search request and filename reference
Name search result printout from e-Registry
Business scope narrative coded to ISIC 7810 and NAICS 561330
Trademark clearance opinion if applicable
Identity document or business registration number of the proposed General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If e-Registry flags the name because of a conflicting company or LPF record, immediately file a new name application with alternative proposed names. If trademark opposition is anticipated, request a name rectification under Cap. 637 section 7 and withdraw the objectionable name rather than contest at filing. If a government endorsement is required for a sensitive word, obtain a letter of no objection or change the name before proceeding to Form LPF1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Limited Partnership Agreement and Statutory Officer Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong notary public or solicitor qualified under the Law Society of Hong Kong; no registry filing occurs at this step, but the executed packet is lodged with Companies Registry in Step 3
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft, review, and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement containing the full capital contribution schedule, profit-sharing percentages, management authority of the General Partner, limited partner restrictions, a foreign-invested ownership schedule, and an express election that the Limited Partnership Fund regime of Cap. 637 applies. Have each partner execute signature pages in counterpart; if a corporate partner acts, that corporate partner must pass a certified board resolution and attach a certificate of good standing. The General Partner must sign a statutory declaration verifying that all information is true and that no false statement has been made. Statutory officers, being the General Partner, Responsible Person, AML/CFT compliance officer, and Employment Agency Authorized Representative, must execute consents to act. Have the notary public witness the execution and, where required by the funding jurisdiction, apostille or legalize the execution packet for the Mainland China ultimate investor. Preserve original notarized copies for Companies Registry scrutiny and bank KYC.
required_dossiers: Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Capital contribution schedule
Statutory declaration of compliance signed by the General Partner
Consents to act by General Partner and AML/CFT Responsible Person
Corporate documents for any corporate partner including board resolution, certificate of incorporation, and certificate of good standing
Notarial certificate and apostille or legalization letter for the foreign investor
Registered office consent and landlord approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any notary or counsel identifies an inconsistency between the Limited Partnership Agreement and Cap. 637, amend the agreement by a signed supplemental deed and re-execute before a notary before lodging. If a corporate partner's certificate of good standing is stale, obtain a renewed certificate from the local registry and submit a cover letter explaining the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Form LPF1 and Registration of the Hong Kong Foreign-Invested Partnership with Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Limited Partnerships Fund Unit, e-Registry electronic filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Registry e-Registry platform, complete and validate Form LPF1 with the exact Limited Partnership Agreement details, registered office, General Partner, Responsible Person, capital amount, and business description aligned to ISIC 7810 and NAICS 561330. Attach scanned copies of the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, statutory declarations, consent forms, registered office consent, and the foreign-invested ownership schedule. Pay the official registration fee using the approved electronic payment method and retrieve the electronic acknowledgement. Monitor the file for requisitions and do not commence payroll activity until the Certificate of Registration and Business Registration Certificate are issued. On approval, the Registry enters the partnership in the Limited Partnerships Fund Register and issues a Certificate of Registration. Verify the name and statutory details on the certificate immediately and notify the Companies Registry of any discrepancy within seven days.
required_dossiers: Form LPF1 signed by the General Partner
Notarized Limited Partnership Agreement
Statutory declaration of compliance
Consents to act of statutory officers
Registered office consent and proof of address
Foreign-invested ownership schedule and beneficial ownership chart
Payment receipt for the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a requisition, submit a supplementary response explaining any mismatch and file a corrected Form LPF1 within fourteen days. If the application is refused, re-file with a changed name or amended Limited Partnership Agreement under Cap. 637 section 5, or pursue the applicable appeal or judicial review remedy within the permitted statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Employment Agency Licence, and Premises Fire and Workplace Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department; Employment Agencies Administration of the Labour Department; Fire Services Department; Buildings Department for means-of-escape and structural clearance of the office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after registration, file Form IRBR1 to obtain a Business Registration Certificate from the Inland Revenue Department, and apply for the Employment Agency Licence under section 50 of the Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57). For the agency licence, submit fit-and-proper person declarations for the Authorized Representative, an approved fee schedule, standard services terms for EOR and payroll clients, and evidence that the office premises comply with fire safety and occupancy requirements. Request a fire service inspection from the Fire Services Department where the office is a shared commercial premises or exceeds the simple office occupancy threshold. Obtain a Fire Service Installations and Equipment Certificate and Buildings Department compliance approval for means of escape and structural loading if the premises are in a multi-tenant building. Do not advertise EOR services or place contractors until both the Business Registration Certificate and the Employment Agency Licence are physically displayed at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Form IRBR1
Limited Partnership Fund Certificate of Registration
Employment Agency Licence application form
Fit-and-proper person declarations for the Authorized Representative
EOR client and worker services contract templates
Fee schedule and payroll services terms
Office lease and floor plan
Fire service installations and equipment certificate or letter of compliance
Buildings Department approval for means of escape
Building management approval for use as an employment agency
Criminal record declaration or clearance for the Authorized Representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Labour Department raises fit-and-proper objections, substitute another authorized representative and resubmit the licence application. If the fire certificate is pending, remedy the fire safety defect notice and apply for a provisional or conditional licence. If the Business Registration application is queried, provide supplementary income tax, tenancy, and ownership proof to the Business Registration Office within the prescribed response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Payroll, Banking, Tax, MPF, and AML Activation for Global EOR Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department for employer registration; Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority for MPF registration; Hong Kong Monetary Authority-regulated bank for Local Payroll Direct Debit and Wise rails; Companies Registry for ongoing LPF compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the partnership bank account at the approved bank and complete KYC with the Limited Partnership Fund certificate, notarized Limited Partnership Agreement, Business Registration Certificate, beneficial ownership chart, and evidence of the designated payment rails. Register as an employer with the Inland Revenue Department using the prescribed IR56 notification forms before the first employee is engaged. Enroll all eligible employees in a registered Mandatory Provident Fund scheme within the statutory enrolment period and obtain an employer participation certificate. Purchase Employees' Compensation insurance policy covering all EOR and contracted workers. Establish AML/CFT controls including sanctions screening, source-of-funds verification, and transaction monitoring for the payroll rails. Maintain the registered office signboard, statutory registers, and annual return calendar. File the LPF annual return with the Companies Registry as required and preserve all records for seven years.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of the Limited Partnership Fund
Business Registration Certificate
Bank KYC pack including resolution and signatory list
Beneficial ownership and ultimate PRC parent chart
MPF employer participation certificate
Employees' Compensation insurance policy
IRD employer registration notifications
AML/CFT compliance manual and risk assessment
Annual return Form LPF2 calendar and draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial ownership documentation, provide a notarized beneficial ownership chart and an updated certificate of good standing for the corporate partner. If the MPF scheme provider refuses enrolment, request assistance from the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority. If the Inland Revenue Department flags late employer registration, make a voluntary disclosure with mitigating reasons and pay any prescribed late filing fee within twenty-one days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Labour Department - Employment Agencies Administration for the statutory manpower service licence; Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department for commercial operation; Fire Services Department and Buildings Department for office premises clearance; no separate industrial licensing authority arises for ISIC 7810

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China acting through the National Electronic Tax Service portal; for Hong Kong SAR, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) through the eTax portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The foreign investor files the establishment application with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or its local counterpart to register the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP); upon approval, the FIP receives a business license and a Uniform Social Credit Code (USCC). Step 2: Within 30 days after the business license is issued, the FIP completes taxpayer registration through the provincial State Taxation Administration (STA) e-Tax service; the USCC becomes the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for e-filing and VAT purposes. Step 3: If a foreign partner is a non-resident enterprise without a Chinese establishment, a non-resident enterprise tax record must be established under the Administrative Measures for Tax Registration of Non-Resident Enterprises, either directly at the STA office exercising jurisdiction over the payer or via the e-tax platform, to support withholding, services, dividends, royalties, and other China-source income compliance. Step 4: The FIP must apply for a digital certificate (CA key) for the electronic tax system to enable authorized online declarations and payments. Step 5: If the FIP also maintains a Hong Kong business registration presence, the IRD Business Registration Office will issue a Business Registration Certificate (BRC); for Hong Kong profits tax and filing obligations, the IRD eTax system is used.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for income-tax classification. A Chinese Foreign-Invested Partnership is fiscally transparent by default for enterprise income tax purposes; there is no check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election available under Chinese domestic law. For VAT purposes, the FIP may elect small-scale taxpayer simplified treatment until annual taxable turnover exceeds the mandatory general taxpayer threshold. Hong Kong does not provide a check-the-box election for this entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) in China; Hong Kong SAR has no general VAT, GST, or sales tax regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: China VAT: mandatory general taxpayer registration is triggered when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000; all active enterprises must complete basic tax registration from business commencement regardless of turnover. Hong Kong: no VAT registration threshold because no VAT/GST exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the State Taxation Administration's Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice system under the Golden Tax System Phase IV architecture; VAT invoices must be issued through STA-approved electronic channels, transmitted in near real-time to the tax authority's clearance platform, and authenticated with unique invoice numbers and digital anti-fraud stamps. Hong Kong does not impose a corresponding general real-time fiscal clearance or e-invoicing mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under China VAT rules, exported goods are zero-rated when they are declared to China Customs and physically leave Chinese territory. Cross-border services, including international EOR and payroll support provided to an overseas principal, may qualify for zero-rating or VAT exemption if the service is consumed wholly outside China, the recipient is located outside China, and the transaction satisfies the statutory place-of-supply and beneficial enjoyment conditions. The zero-rated supply must be supported by a fully digitalized zero-rated VAT invoice and documented evidence of foreign currency settlement received in China.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration (Bill of Entry) duly accepted by China Customs
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving the goods physically left Chinese territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank foreign-exchange receipt voucher
Cross-border service agreement or EOR staffing contract with the overseas principal
Place-of-supply and beneficial owner evidence, including service completion records, milestone reports, and payroll timesheets
Zero-rated VAT invoice issued through the Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to strict audit scrutiny. If the supporting documentation is incomplete, false, or the services are found not to be genuinely consumed outside China, the zero-rating is reversed and the tax authority will claw back the unpaid VAT plus a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day. Administrative penalties may range from 50% to 500% of the tax shortfall under the Tax Administration Law of the People's Republic of China. Fraudulent export tax refund claims may also trigger criminal liability, unlimited statutory recovery periods, and imprisonment under the PRC Criminal Law provisions governing tax fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), acting under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Hong Kong SAR operates as a separate monetary jurisdiction with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as its de facto central bank and the Hong Kong dollar (HKD) freely convertible under the linked exchange rate system. However, because the subject entity is a Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) formed in mainland China with cross-border payments into and out of Hong Kong, the relevant foreign exchange control authority for RMB current and capital account items is the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) in the People's Republic of China. RMB is not freely convertible on the capital account; capital injections into the FIP require SAFE registration, foreign exchange quota approval, and conversion through a designated domestic bank under the Foreign Invested Partnership foreign exchange registration regime. Current account items such as trade-related service fees, payroll disbursements, management fees, and employer-of-record service fees are generally convertible upon submission of authentic supporting documentation (contracts, invoices, customs or service verification), but the payer must complete a SAFE 'Direct Reporting' transaction code and retain full documentary trails for five years. Profit remittances and dividend-like distributions from the FIP to non-resident partners require an annual audit report, tax payment proof (corporate income tax withholding where applicable), and a SAFE foreign exchange payment application, making outbound distributions subject to material administrative friction. Surrender requirements apply to export proceeds for goods trade, but for a staffing agency primarily exporting services, foreign currency receipts derived from cross-border service revenue must be repatriated and converted into RMB according to the prevailing SAFE rules unless a verified offshore retention account is approved. The Hong Kong receiving entity is unrestricted in holding and deploying HKD and foreign currency liquidity, and may aggregate global EOR payroll liquidity in Hong Kong as a treasury hub, provided that onshore RMB funding flows into China are properly structured as current account service payments with underlying employment contracts and payroll agency agreements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For service-export proceeds received into mainland China, the FIP must repatriate receipts to its domestic SAFE-designated foreign exchange settlement account within the statutory timeline (generally within 180 days of receipt for current account items or as stipulated in the registration certificate, unless an extension is approved for bona fide commercial reasons). The mandatory conversion ratio historically was 100 percent surrender for allowable export receipts under the old rules; after SAFE reforms, enterprises may retain receipts in foreign currency accounts or convert voluntarily, but capital verification and RMB funding for operational expenses typically require settlement at the prevailing spot rate through the designated bank, with all transactions reported under the correct service trade code such as 'payroll and employment services' or 'management consulting services' in the SAFE digital monitoring system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (HKD and RMB multi-currency account)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Foreign Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (Asia) Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Treasury Account with RMB clearing capability
Basic Operational Account for payroll and payroll agent settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs and neobanks such as Wise (TransferWise) are not licensed to provide regulated corporate banking services to mainland China onshore entities, and cannot serve as the primary settlement bank for the FIP's domestic RMB obligations, SAFE-registered capital flows, or tax payment processes in China. Their viability in Hong Kong is higher: licensed stored value facilities or money service operators may be used for low-value global payroll disbursements, but they remain supplementary because they do not offer full corporate credit lines, trade finance, SAFE-compliant RMB conversion, or capital account intermediation. For the global EOR staffing agency treasury structure, the recommended approach is a hybrid: use a tier-1 Hong Kong licensed bank as the core liquidity clearing and payroll disbursement hub, and use Wise only for marginal non-regulated beneficiary payments in corridors where FX efficiency matters, provided the Hong Kong entity is the contractual payor and each remittance has underlying payroll or contractor agreements to satisfy AML screening.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Hong Kong-incorporated entity opening accounts with tier-1 banks, physical presence of statutory directors is generally mandated for the initial onboarding interview, typically requiring all directors, the company secretary, and the ultimate beneficial owner to appear in-branch (or via the bank's prescribed secure video verification for select jurisdictions). Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for the initial account-opening interview. For the mainland China FIP, physical presence of the general partner or designated authorized signatory is also mandatory at the mainland SAFE-designated bank branch for foreign exchange registration, capital account opening, and evidentiary verification. The Hong Kong subsidiary of the global EOR platform should therefore plan a bank-visited onboarding session in Hong Kong for all directors and final beneficial owners, and separately authorize the mainland FIP general partner to complete in-person SAFE registration in China.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity for a multi-tier Hong Kong and mainland Chinese structure with foreign partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart showing all intermediate holding vehicles, certified copies of certificates of incorporation, partnership agreements, register of partners, UBO declarations for every individual holding 25 percent or more of ownership or control, source-of-wealth statements and bank references for each UBO, and a notarized statutory declaration confirming the funding sources for the initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual jurisdiction payroll flow with cross-border employee/contractor payments and potential red flags of unlicensed money transmission
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive Global EOR client agreements, underlying employment contracts or independent contractor agreements, payroll calculation ledgers, social insurance and tax filing evidence in China and Hong Kong, a list of destination countries with local payroll licenses, and targeted AML policies including transaction monitoring rules that flag velocity anomalies, bunching, and round-tripping of payroll funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of digital EMI / Wise payment rails creating non-bank settlement concentration risk and third-party payment trigger points
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury governance policy evidencing that the Fintech EMI is restricted to low-value, high-frequency payroll transactions below a specified threshold; contractual terms with the EMI confirming no corporate lending or virtual asset activities; a daily reconciliation process; and a sub-ledger mapping each remittance to the underlying beneficiary with supporting time-and-attendance or contractor performance records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent business activity risk due to low-tax Hong Kong jurisdiction combined with mainland China service revenue generation, raising BEPS and substance concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic substance documentation including physical Hong Kong office lease, local payroll and HR headcount, board meeting minutes in Hong Kong, management decision files, transfer pricing documentation (master file and local file) evidencing arm's length EOR fees, Hong Kong profits tax returns, and contemporaneous service records proving that value-added functions and control are actually performed in Hong Kong.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the mainland China FIP must be routed through a SAFE-registered foreign exchange settlement account at a tier-1 Chinese commercial bank (e.g., Bank of China Shanghai branch) using the following protocol: (1) execute the FIP partnership agreement and obtain the business license; (2) complete SAFE foreign exchange establishment registration for the FIP and obtain the Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate; (3) effect the wire transfer from the Hong Kong treasury company through SWIFT MT103 citing purpose code 'grant of other equity capital' (currently aligned with SAFE classification 622081 for investment inward remittance) or the appropriate capital project code; (4) ensure the remitter is the registered foreign partner and the beneficiary is the FIP's capital escrow account; (5) upon receipt, the domestic bank will conduct capital verification through a certified public accountant and issue a capital verification report confirming the foreign exchange settlement and RMB conversion; and (6) convert foreign currency into RMB using a SAFE-designated spot transaction, ensuring compliance with the negative list and the Foreign Investment Law negative list restrictions (the staffing agency industry should be analyzed against the latest market entry negative list, though HR and EOR services are generally permitted unless involving specific Chinese listing or dispatch licensing thresholds). The Hong Kong paying entity must maintain all originator and beneficiary details, remittance contracts, and underlying partnership agreements for five years to satisfy bank replay queries.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound global payroll and EOR disbursements from the Hong Kong treasury hub, the recommended clearing rails are: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct beneficiary payments to employee bank accounts and contractor accounts in countries outside mainland China, with full structured remittance information (employee name, payroll reference, contract number, and purpose code 'wages, salaries, and other remuneration'); (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) are not appropriate for payroll, but may be used only if the EOR platform engages in procurement of software or tangible goods ancillary to staffing services; for such goods, a confirmed irrevocable documentary credit opened by the Hong Kong entity from a tier-1 bank provides settlement security; and (c) Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) are viable only for trade-based invoices to corporate clients for recruitment or workforce management services, but for pure payroll pass-through flows the SWIFT MT103 credit transfer rail is the dominant, lowest-risk method; use professional clearing via the HK Clearing House Automated Transfer System (CHATS) in HKD and USD, concurrent with RMB clearing via the Hong Kong RMB Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system for onward transfers to mainland China.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forwards for period up to 12 months available to the FIP from a SAFE-designated domestic bank, requiring real trade or settlement background and the submission of the underlying service or payroll contract for the bank's authenticity review.

Hong Kong non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNH for hedging RMB exposure without onshore SAFE registration, permissible for the Hong Kong entity as an offshore participant with maturity generally up to 2 years.

Currency swaps between HKD, USD, RMB, and other payroll currencies for cross-currency treasury matching, executed only with licensed counterparties under ISDA documentation, ensuring that no derivative transaction creates a leveraged speculative exposure contrary to SAFE's derivatives real-demand principle.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Registration Certificate Renewal (Business Registration Office Form IRBR1 / Payment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal must be lodged on or before the expiry date of the current certificate (typically one year from registration anniversary); a one-month late window exists before escalated late fees are applied.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a fixed late fee of HK$3,000; continuing failure to renew exposes the proprietor to prosecution and fines of HK$5,000 plus treble the outstanding fee and levy; trading without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence. If the certificate is cancelled after successive non-renewal, the Inland Revenue Department will notify the Companies Registry, which may administratively strike off the entity and cause assets to be held in abeyance for the Government.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after the anniversary date of incorporation (the 'return date')
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late delivery is subject to escalating registration fees: HK$870 (delivered more than 42 days but not more than 3 months), HK$1,740 (3–6 months), HK$2,610 (6–9 months), HK$3,480 (more than 9 months). The company and each responsible officer are liable to prosecution; if a company defaults on annual return obligations for an extended period, the Companies Registry may invoke strike-off powers, resulting in dissolution and the Crown's entitlement to the company's assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Partnership/Corporation with EOR trading income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Profits Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within one month from the date of issue of the return (extended due dates, if any, will be stated on the return; electronic filing may receive a further extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing results in an estimated assessment with a 10% additional tax surcharge under Inland Revenue Ordinance s.82A; a default summons may impose a fine up to HK$50,000 plus HK$5,000 for each month of continued default; willful evasion carries fines of up to HK$100,000 and imprisonment of up to 2 years. Persistent non-filing does not strike off the entity but could lead to deregistration by the Business Registration Office after 12 months inactive.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration & Pensions (Form IR56B) for EOR/Payroll Staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the issue date of the Employer's Return pack; in practice on or before 30 April/5 May following the 31 March year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing of IR56B is an offence under s.80(1) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, with a fine up to HK$10,000 and 6 months imprisonment for each offence; the department may also raise additional tax assessments for staff and penalize the employer up to double the understated tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employment Agency Licence Renewal (EOR staffing and contractor payroll agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application must be submitted before the expiry of the current employment agency licence (valid for one year); applications should be lodged at least 30 days prior to expiry to avoid interruption.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Carrying on an employment agency without a valid licence is a criminal offence punishable on conviction by a fine of HK$350,000 and imprisonment for up to 3 years. The Commissioner for Labour may also refuse to renew or may cancel the licence, in which case the entity must cease payroll/placement operations immediately.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Independent Auditor's Report (annual statutory audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (submitted with Profits Tax Return); shareholders/partners; Companies Registry where an audit exemption or dispensation is not claimed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a private company or foreign-invested partnership under HK GAAP: within 6 months after the financial year-end; for tax purposes the audited accounts must accompany the Profits Tax Return by its statutory due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have audited financial statements does not attract a separate registry fee, but the IRD may reject the tax return, raise estimated assessments with a 10% penalty surcharge, and impose fines for non-compliance. A licensed employment agency failing to evidence a solvent and audited position may have its Employment Agency Licence revoked by the Labour Department; partners/directors may also risk disqualification orders.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: In the HKSAR there is no statutory balance-sheet, gross turnover, or headcount threshold above which an audit is first triggered; instead, under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every active Hong Kong incorporated company (including a private company limited by shares and an unlimited company with a separate audit requirement) must be audited annually by a certified public accountant, except a company that validly claims dormant status under section 359 and files Form NDRC9. A 'Foreign-Invested Partnership' structured under HK law is not exempt merely because it is a limited partnership; the IRD expects accounts in support of the Partnership Return, and if the entity is registered as a Limited Partnership Fund (LPF) under the Limited Partnership Funds Ordinance, the LPF must appoint an independent auditor and file audited financial statements annually. Additional heavy-touch triggers applicable to a Global EOR/staffing agency: (i) holding client monies or funds in trust requires an independent audit of client assets under the Employment Ordinance and AML requirements; (ii) a bank lending covenant will invariably require audited financial statements above HK$1,000,000 in borrowing facilities; and (iii) any public-interest status or third-party stakeholder reliance creates professional and fiduciary obligations calling for audited consolidated/entity accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) as issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), aligned with IFRS. Private entities and owner-managed partnerships may adopt the HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE) framework where they are not publicly accountable and are not required to use full HKFRS; separate financial statements must nevertheless comply with Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s. 380, and the independent audit must be performed under Hong Kong Standards on Auditing (HKSAs).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong maintains a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) for companies at the registered office, and the register must be physically available for inspection at all times. There is no annual 'confirmation statement' or UBO return filed with the Companies Registry; however, on formation and at each annual return preparation the company must identify and record significant controllers, and every change in significant control must be noted within 7 days of the company becoming aware of it, with the SCR updated within 7 days. For a limited partnership under Cap. 37, changes of general partner, registered address, contribution, and allocation ratios must be registered with the Companies Registry within 7 days on Form LP-4. For a Hong Kong company, any issue/allotment of shares must be filed on Form NSC1 within 1 month of the allotment, and transfer instruments must be stamped by the Inland Revenue Department within 30 days of execution (Hong Kong stamp duty is ad valorem for shares) and then duly recorded in the Register of Members.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Register of Partners
Minute Book (and written resolutions of shareholders/partners)
Register of Share Allotments and Transfers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,400 - USD 4,800 per year (professional corporate-services and registered-office provider for a Hong Kong FIP/EOR platform)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 - USD 14,000 per audit (certified independent CPA audit dependent on payroll headcount, transaction volume, multi-state employer obligations, and trust-account review)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% standard rate for unincorporated businesses/partnerships (two-tiered profits tax: 7.5% on first HKD 2 million assessable profits; 15% on remainder)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial source principle: only profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong are taxable; offshore profits claimable as non-taxable. No VAT/GST, no capital gains tax, no dividend withholding tax. Enhanced R&D tax deduction: 300% on first HKD 2 million of qualifying R&D expenditure and 200% on the remainder. All taxes are based on self-assessment; no withholding on distributions to partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory limit (carryforward indefinite at partner level, subject to source and business continuity rules)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return – Partnerships (BIR52) filed via the Hong Kong eTAX portal (GovHK electronic filing system)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 1 month from the issue date (usually first working day of April). For accounting period ending 31 December, automatic extension to 15 August for direct filing, or 15 November with tax representative. Other accounting periods may apply for extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business name, Business Registration Number, principal place of business, and nature of business (ISIC 7810 – Global EOR and staffing agency)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the BRN and business address match the Business Registration Office records. If the partnership claims offshore profits, describe the operational structure in Hong Kong. Non-resident partners must provide their tax identification numbers and country of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period – start/end dates of the accounting year (usually 1 January to 31 December)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All partners must adopt the same basis period. If the financial statements are prepared to a date other than 31 December, the IRD may issue a short-period assessment. Non-resident partners must report their share based on the HK basis period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit / (loss) per financial statements, before tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate all EOR service fees from global clients. Translate foreign currency income to HKD at the IRD-approved average exchange rate. Ensure intercompany fees reflect arm's length prices for transfer pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add: disallowable expenses (e.g., depreciation, private expenditure, property tax, profits tax paid and foreign taxes paid, and dividends paid to limited partners)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any management or service fees paid to offshore related companies must be deducted at the arm's length amount; excessive fees may be disallowed proportionally. Non-resident partners cannot claim personal deductions against partnership income unless permitted by the HK tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct: allowable expenses not charged in accounts (e.g., capital allowances, donations, approved scientific research expenditure)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capital allowances on plant and machinery are allocated among partners in profit-sharing ratios. For non-resident partners, the asset must be used in Hong Kong for generating assessable profits; if an asset is used partly offshore, a proportionate claim is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable profits / (adjusted loss) before allocation to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule showing each partner's share of assessable profits (including non-resident partners). Non-resident partners must use this schedule to complete their own IRD filings (BIR55 for individuals, BIR51 for corporate partners). If profits are claimed offshore, the partnership must file an offshore claim with supporting evidence (contracts, employee locations, payment flows).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without reasonable excuse: HKD 10,000 fine (IRO s.80) and possible additional tax of 3 times undercharged. For willful tax evasion (IRO s.82): HKD 50,000 fine and up to 3 years' imprisonment (summary) or 5 years (indictment) plus 3 times tax. IRD may issue estimated assessments and impose s.82A additional penalties (10% of undercharged tax). Continued non-compliance may result in summons, blacklisting, and travel ban.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – Hong Kong does not impose dividend withholding tax on any distribution. In a partnership, no deemed dividend applies; profits are allocated directly and taxed at partner level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: As HK does not levy dividend WHT, no DTA relief is required for HK-source dividends. For income from Mainland China, the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA provides reduced WHT (dividends as low as 5% if beneficial owner is a company holding at least 25% capital; otherwise 10%). To claim DTA relief, the Hong Kong resident partner must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the IRD (Form IR1313A via eTAX), submit the appropriate application to the Mainland tax authority (e.g., Form S or approval filing), and provide beneficial ownership evidence (economic substance, board resolutions, and explanation of income flow). A transparent partnership is generally not a resident 'person' under the DTA; each partner must rely on their own TRC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Hong Kong does not impose WHT on royalties or interest paid to non-residents. For China-source royalty and interest, PRC statutory WHT is 10%, reduced to 7% under the DTA subject to TRC and beneficial ownership. Royalty payments for intangibles (e.g., EOR software) may also attract PRC VAT at 6% plus surtaxes. Intercompany interest paid by a HK FIP to an overseas shareholder may be subject to thin capitalization rules if applicable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under HK Inland Revenue Ordinance, a taxpayer must prepare a Local File if the annual turnover exceeds HKD 500 million and the aggregate amount of controlled transactions exceeds HKD 100 million. A Master File is required if the MNE group has consolidated revenue of at least HKD 6.8 billion. Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue ≥ HKD 6.8 billion and operations in multiple jurisdictions. These thresholds apply to partnerships where controlled transactions are conducted with associated enterprises.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Hong Kong has no codified Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) like traditional offshore centres. However, under the territorial source principle and IRO s.61A general anti-avoidance rule, taxpayers claiming offshore income treatment must demonstrate that Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) (for an EOR: client acquisition, contract negotiation, payroll processing, employee onboarding/compliance, and risk management) are performed outside Hong Kong. If the CIGA are performed in Hong Kong, the corresponding profits will be taxable onshore. A mere shell bookkeeping arrangement will be disregarded, and profits will be adjusted to reflect the substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Misrepresentation of Offshore Profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP claims all EOR profits as offshore and exempt by executing the main service contracts with a zero-tax jurisdiction affiliate while in fact all key personnel, payroll systems, and bank accounts are located in Hong Kong, thereby deliberately understating Hong Kong-source profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upon conviction under IRO s.82: fine up to HKD 50,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years (summary conviction) or up to 5 years (indictment), in addition to a further fine of 3 times the tax undercharged. The IRD may also impose a s.82A additional tax of 10% of the undercharged tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing general partner (or director-equivalent) is personally and criminally liable if they signed the false return or directed the arrangement. Civil liability includes repayment of all avoided tax and penalties; assets can be charged under a court order. A departure ban (travel ban / blacklist) may be issued under IRO s.80H. Imprisonment terms as per sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP has no physical office in Hong Kong, no locally employed staff, and its only activity is circulating payroll via Wise through a Hong Kong bank account, while actual EOR management and control are exercised from an offshore jurisdiction, forming a sham arrangement to avoid HK profits tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRO s.61A permits the IRD to disregard the arrangement and recharacterise profits as onshore, subject to tax at the top rate. Additionally, a penalty of 10% of the tax undercharged is imposed under s.82A. If the sham is found to be fraudulent trading, the Companies Court may wind up the entity and impose fines under the Companies Ordinance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The partner may be personally liable for the full tax and penalties; the court may order restitution of the assets extracted from the partnership. Director disqualification up to 15 years could occur if fraudulent trading is proven. A travel ban and blacklisting by the IRD may be issued, and the partner could be subject to criminal imprisonment for up to 5 years under s.56C of the Crimes Ordinance if fraud is committed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Compliance Failure in Global Payroll Channel
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP, acting as an EOR, fails to conduct customer due diligence on its foreign clients, does not maintain beneficial ownership records, and uses Wise for cross-border salary payments without transaction monitoring, thereby concealing the origin of funds or facilitating money laundering through the payroll rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cap. 615 (AMLO) s.21 – failure to apply CDD measures: fine up to HKD 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years per offence; continued non-compliance may attract a daily penalty. The company may be deregistered/relicensed. If laundering is established, the proceeds of crime act may impose additional fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/general partners can be criminally prosecuted for wilful neglect of AML duties; they face the full fine and imprisonment (up to 2 years). They may be collectively and severally liable for compensable losses, and asset restraint orders can be issued under the Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance. A travel ban and blacklisting by the banking sector are practical consequences, with potential extradition if funds involved foreign criminal proceeds.
